hypotheses.reasoning: The trigger was small: template-svc-3 failed its liveness probe and restarted at 23:02:24 (#96), cutting capacity to 3/4. It was back at 4/4 by 23:02:59 (#99). Right after that, notification-svc's TemplateClient began retrying 503s immediately with backoff disabled, up to 4 attempts (#101, #106, #111). That multiplied inbound load on template-svc to 3.2x and then 4.1x baseline (#110, #118), so template-svc kept shedding load with 503s (#105, #121, #132). This loop feeds itself, which is why the gateway 503s on /v1/notify continue after the instance recovered. There are no deploys in the window, and the poison message at 22:52 (#17) went to the DLQ without causing harm.
Another reading is that template-svc is simply short on capacity and its queue fills up. But load only rose after the retries started, and capacity was fully restored.
A message failed schema validation and was moved to the DLQ 10 minutes before the onset. The worker kept processing normally afterwards, so this is unrelated.

verdict.recommendedAction: Turn on exponential backoff with jitter and a retry budget or circuit breaker in notification-svc's TemplateClient (or temporarily turn retries off). Then add short-term template-svc capacity or rate limiting so the backlog clears. Later, find out why template-svc-3 failed its liveness probe.
